claim_text: Dropbox's status page opened an incident at 2:28 PM ET on Nov 20 and marked it resolved at 3:13 PM ET
summary: Dropbox posted an incident titled 'Dropbox is not working as expected for some users' at 2:28 PM ET (19:28 UTC) on Friday, Nov 20. It said a fix was in place at 3:05 PM and marked the incident resolved at 3:13 PM, about 45 minutes in all.
detail: Dropbox's updates were: Investigating (2:28 PM), a further update (2:37 PM), Monitoring (3:05 PM), Resolved (3:13 PM). The times are the status page's own, converted from UTC. The page gives no detail beyond that.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Dropbox's own status page lists each update with its time; Technobezz relays the same times.

claim_text: The status page rated the incident Critical, with the website, apps and API in major outage
summary: Dropbox's status page rates the incident's impact as Critical. Twelve components were in major outage: the website, desktop and mobile apps, API, Paper, Passwords, Dash, Protect, Replay, DocSend, MCP Server and Support Services.
detail: All twelve returned to operational at 3:13 PM ET. Dropbox Sign is not among the components on the status page, so we do not list it as affected. The status page says only that some users were affected and gives no figure.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The incident page's component list and impact rating are Dropbox's own; Technobezz lists the same components.

claim_text: Dropbox said the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or by AI acting on its own
summary: In its 2:37 PM ET update, Dropbox wrote: 'The outage is not caused by a cyberattack or by AI acting on its own.' It posted this while still investigating.
detail: This confirms what Dropbox said, not an independent finding. The wording rules out a cyberattack and AI acting on its own; it does not say whether any AI tool or any change by Dropbox staff played a part. No regulator, CISA or outside researcher has commented that we found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The statement is on Dropbox's own status page, a Tier 1 primary source; Technobezz and UptimeRobot repeat it.

claim_text: The outage was not a cyberattack
summary: No source outside Dropbox has confirmed or contradicted Dropbox's statement that the outage was not a cyberattack.
detail: Dropbox's statement was made 9 minutes after it opened the incident and before it said what the cause was. The outlets that carry it repeat the status page.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Every account of the denial traces back to Dropbox's status page; no independent source speaks to the cause.

claim_text: The root cause of the outage
summary: Dropbox has not said what caused the outage. Its status page names no cause, and we found no post-incident report.
detail: The fix is described only as 'a fix has been implemented'.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The incident page has four short updates and none gives a cause.

summary: Dropbox says 'some users' were affected and gives no number or region.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The status page does not size the impact.

claim_text: The White House said on Nov 18 it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind recent tech outages; it did not name Dropbox
summary: A Nov 18 White House release quotes the DNI and the National Security Adviser seeing no indication of a coordinated cyberattack behind recent tech outages and no evidence the incidents are related.
detail: The release came two days before the Dropbox outage and does not mention Dropbox, so it is context, not a finding about Dropbox. It confirms what officials said, not an independent finding.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The release is the primary document and carries the quotes.

claim_text: The Dropbox outage is linked to this month's other outages
summary: No source we found links the Dropbox outage to the FAA, Microsoft 365, Apple, Workday or other outages of recent weeks.
detail: Dropbox's status page mentions no other company or event. Dropbox posted its own separate incident, and its Nov 17 'Sign in with Apple' incident is a different, earlier event.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing in Dropbox's updates or the White House release connects them.
